evals.prompt: Define cron scheduling as this skill teaches it. Your answer must include schedule expression, trigger surface, authenticated entrypoint, durable execution target, idempotency, and observability.
Explain the alarm-clock-to-factory mental model for cron scheduling and name the reliability envelope around the trigger.
Why is a cron job that runs twice or fails silently dangerous? Name the design checks this skill uses to prevent those failures.

A user asks how to move a slow user-triggered export out of an API route and report progress. Which part belongs to background-jobs, which part would belong to cron-scheduling only if present, and why?

Classify these concerns as cron-scheduling, background-jobs, observability, or webhook-integration: UTC schedule, CRON_SECRET authorization, duplicate scheduled invocations, worker retry policy, heartbeat alert, incoming provider event schema.
Use the alarm-clock-to-factory analogy to explain why a cron route should usually dispatch durable work rather than perform long-running logic inline.

Novel scenario: a Vercel Cron route runs every five minutes, performs an eight-minute sync inline, catches errors and returns 200, and has no idempotency table. Apply the skill to identify every failure mode and propose a corrected architecture.
